title: Dissolved salt makes ocean water denser than pure water
summary: Dissolved material makes a given volume of water heavier, so ocean water with salt in it is denser than pure water.
body: The U.S. Geological Survey says the density of water also depends on what is dissolved in it. Water in nature holds minerals, gases, salts, and other material. As more material is dissolved in a gallon, that gallon weighs more and is more dense. The page draws the everyday conclusion that ocean water, which contains dissolved salt, is denser than pure water. Ice floating in that salty water is a different claim, on the floating card. No salinity table is copied here.
